source: Atomic Structure Moles and the Periodic Table (Baldivis, 2019)
text: Why is the relative atomic mass on the periodic table a decimal?
html: Why is the relative atomic mass on the periodic table a decimal?
answerHtml:
Supplied key: A.

It is the average of the abundance and mass of all of the isotopes of the element.
options: It is the average of the abundance and mass of all of the isotopes of the element.
It is the average of the abundance and mass of all of the allotropes of the element.
It depends on the percentage abundance of the element in the Earth’s crust.
It depends on which atom of carbon the element is being compared to.
optionsHtml: It is the average of the abundance and mass of all of the isotopes of the element.
